G3985I.as:
πειράζω, poët. and late prose form of πειράω, q.v., [in LXX for נסה pi.;]
1. to make proof of (Hom.).
2. to try, attempt (Luc., Polyb., al.): c. inf. (v. M, Pr., 205; Bl., § 69, 4), .
3. In LXX and NT, like Heb. נסה, c. acc. pers., to test, try, prove;
(a) in a good sense: , , , ; esp. of trials and afflictions sent or permitted by God (Ge 22:1, Ex 20:20, Wi 3:5, al.), , , , ;
(b) in a bad sense (Apoll. Rhod., 3, 10): of the attempts made to ensnare Jesus in his speech, , , , , ; of temptation to sin, to tempt, , (v. Hort, in l.), , ; esp. of temptations of the devil, , , , , , ; ὁ πειράζων, the tempter, , ;
(c) in bad sense also (Ex 17:2, 7, Nu 14:22, al.), of distrustful testing, trying or challenging of God: , (WH, mg., ἐξεπείρασαν), ; τ. πνεῦμα Κυρίου, (cf. ἐκ-πειράζω).†
SYN.: δοκιμάζω, q.v.
